eli5.text: Nothing for you to see or do here this is mainly housekeeping. The team simply stamped a new release number on the download so that people installing or updating get the latest bundle of changes from the past couple of days, none of which are new in this commit. What actually shipped in this release is already live: the AI assistant no longer leaks your IP address to one of its external service providers, a previously-failing coding tool now correctly hides its private files on Linux, and one of the premium AI models got cheaper (its price dropped to zero).

entries.title: New slash command /byok
entries.summary: New slash commands: `/byok`. New files: `cli/src/commands/byok.ts`, `cli/src/utils/byok.ts`, `sdk/scripts/qualify-byok-credentials-worker.ts`, `sdk/scripts/qualify-byok-credentials.ts` (+1 more).

ai.title: Add /byok command and direct provider inference
ai.summary: A new `/byok` slash command (aliases `/provider`) lets Freebuff users run inference directly through their own OpenRouter or OpenAI-compatible provider instead of the Freebuff session. The command, implemented in cli/src/commands/byok.ts and registered as Freebuff-only in cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts and cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts, supports list/add/update/validate/select/remove/off subcommands and parses quoted names literally without evaluating shell syntax. Backing storage lives in cli/src/utils/byok.ts (`useByokSelectionStore`, `resolveByokConnection`, `saveSelectedByokConnection`) and sdk/src/byok.ts (`createBunByokConnectionStore`, `ResolvedByokConnection`, `byokCompletionUrl`), which keep keys in OS credential storage or named environment variables and never persist secret values into chat messages or command history. The change ripples through the SDK run path: client.ts, run.ts, impl/agent-runtime.ts, impl/llm.ts, and impl/model-provider.ts thread a run-scoped `byok` connection through `CodebuffClientOptions`, `RunOptions`, and `getModelForRequest`, while run.ts adds a non-secret inference pin to `RunState` so resumed conversations refuse to switch providers mid-turn. Qualification of the native credential adapter is covered by two new scripts under sdk/scripts/.
ai.evidence: New `handleByokCommand` in cli/src/commands/byok.ts (new) with subcommands list/add/update/validate/select/remove/off; backed by cli/src/utils/byok.ts (new) exposing `useByokSelectionStore`, `resolveByokConnection`, `saveSelectedByokConnection`; registered Freebuff-only in cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts and cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts; SDK layer in sdk/src/byok.ts (new) added `createBunByokConnectionStore`, `ResolvedByokConnection`, `byokCompletionUrl`, plus sdk/src/client.ts, sdk/src/run.ts, sdk/src/impl/agent-runtime.ts, sdk/src/impl/llm.ts, sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts carrying `byok` through run config and provider selection; qualification harness added as sdk/scripts/qualify-byok-credentials.ts and sdk/scripts/qualify-byok-credentials-worker.ts (new).
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the rollout plan or whether the native credential store qualification is gated behind a feature flag.

changes.what: /byok command adds direct OpenRouter/OpenAI-compatible inference with local credential storage and literal quoted-name parsing.
Wiring skips auth and Freebuff session admission when a BYOK connection is selected, and reports the provider/model in the idle status bar.
CodebuffClient and run() accept an optional run-scoped byok connection that bypasses the Codebuff backend and validates against the provider directly.
Adds a qualification harness that exercises the production Bun credential adapter across source and compiled Bun runtimes.
Adds an explicit maxContextLength override to compactContext and applies it during history compaction and programmatic steps.

ai.title: Freebucks row intent moves to shared module, handles unavailable
ai.summary: The Freebucks row-intent logic (`freebucksRowIntent` and `FreebucksRowIntent`) moves out of `cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts` into the new shared module `common/src/util/freebuff-model-selection.ts`, which the CLI now re-exports. The shared type gains a new `confirm` variant for freebucks === null (balance refresh unavailable) that requires spending consent before admission, while freebucks === undefined still means no meter. The CLI picker and session hook carry the freebucks block through refusals and post-session synthesis so the meter's wording survives rate-limited and spend-limited responses.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/util/freebuff-model-selection.ts` defines `FreebucksRowIntent` and `freebucksRowIntent()`, which `cli/src/utils/freebucks.ts` now re-exports, replacing its deleted local copy. The new variant branch { kind: 'confirm', price: undefined, walletSpend: undefined } handles freebucks === null (balance refresh unavailable), a state the old local type lacked. `freebuff-model-selector.tsx` and `use-freebuff-session.ts` now consume the shared module and carry the freebucks block through refusals and post-session synthesis.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumers of the new `consent_required` server status beyond the CLI, nor the rollout of the wallet-spend-limit header across providers.

changes.what: New shared module defining `FreebucksRowIntent` and `freebucksRowIntent()` with a null-balance consent variant.
Re-exports `freebucksRowIntent` and `FreebucksRowIntent` from the shared module, deleting the local copy.
Consumes the shared row-intent module and renders the unavailable-balance notice and price-unavailable confirm wording.
Carries the `freebucks` block through refusals and post-session synthesis, and threads the wallet spend limit through session start.
POST admission now sends `FREEBUFF_WALLET_SPEND_LIMIT_HEADER` and recognizes `consent_required` at HTTP 409.
Adds `FreebuffWalletSpendLimit`, `FreebuffWalletConsent`, the `consent_required` admission variant, and null-safe `getFreebucksInfo`.

ai.title: BYOK pin transition rule
ai.summary: run.ts allows hosted-to-BYOK transitions once while blocking BYOK-to-hosted reversals. Prevents credential changes on resumed runs. Scope: SDK only. Detail: previousInference.source 'codebuff' to 'byok' is permitted; other source mismatches fail.

eli5.text: If you've been running tasks using the hosted (platform-provided) inference, you can now switch to your own provider keys exactly once during a resumed run, and after that switch the system will keep using your keys. You can no longer revert from your own provider keys back to hosted inference, and the system will not silently change your credentials while resuming a task that already uses your keys. This rule is live today in the SDK: a transition from hosted to your own provider is allowed once, while any mismatch in keys or provider on a resumed run is blocked.

ai.title: IOS ad placements added to the placements rail
ai.summary: A new `common/src/ads/ios-placements.ts` module defines the iOS ad surface (`IOS_AD_SURFACE = 'ios'`) alongside three native iOS placement slots (`iOS-Chat-After-Assistant-Message`, `iOS-Coding-After-User-Message`, and `iOS-Coding-After-Assistant-Message`) and an `isIOSAdPlacement` predicate. `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts` imports those exports and spreads `IOS_AD_PLACEMENTS` into the `PLACEMENT_SLOTS` table, tagging each slot with `surface: IOS_AD_SURFACE`, available: true, and format: 'inline' as const, so the iOS native inventory is registered as its own attributable surface rather than aliased to a web or CLI slot. The accompanying comment asserts the intent that native inventory keeps its own attribution and is never aliased to a web slot.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/ads/ios-placements.ts` defines IOS_AD_SURFACE = 'ios' as const, `IOS_AD_PLACEMENTS` (three iOS-specific placement ids with labels), and `isIOSAdPlacement(id)` predicate. `common/src/constants/freebuff-placements.ts` imports `IOS_AD_PLACEMENTS` and `IOS_AD_SURFACE` and spreads `IOS_AD_PLACEMENTS.map(({ id }) => ({ id, surface: IOS_AD_SURFACE, available: true, format: 'inline' as const }))` into `PLACEMENT_SLOTS`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which client or serve-path code consumes the new iOS slots or the `isIOSAdPlacement` predicate.

ai.summary: Deleted `cli/src/utils/format-validation-errors-for-message.ts`. This utility handled formatting validation errors for chat messages, including relative path normalization and clickable link generation. Scope limited to CLI utils.

eli5.text: The assistant used to tidy up validation error messages before showing them to you in the CLI chat, wrapping long paths into neat clickable links like “.agents/myproject/file.ts”. That cleanup code has been deleted, so any tool that relied on it to pre-format errors is now missing. If you run the CLI today, you won’t see the polished path links anymore when validation errors appear in your chat session.

ai.title: Add concurrency and slotLimit to session admission refusals
ai.summary: FreebuffSessionAdmissionResponse now includes optional concurrency and slotLimit fields for capacity refusals. This exposes the exact admission bucket and entitlement-derived limit to the client. Older servers omit these fields; clients must not guess limits. Scope: common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant can't start a new session because the service is at full capacity, the refusal message now includes the exact bucket and limit that blocked it, instead of leaving you to guess. This only affects the client that reports capacity refusals; older servers still send the previous message without these details, and clients are expected to treat the new fields as optional rather than assume a limit. The change is already in place.

ai.title: Add yearly billing interval type and tier offer fields
ai.summary: The shared `common` package now exports `FREEBUFF_SUBSCRIPTION_BILLING_INTERVALS` and `FreebuffSubscriptionBillingInterval` from `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts`, alongside a `isFreebuffSubscriptionBillingInterval` type guard. The offer shape `FreebuffSubscriptionTierOffer` gains an optional `yearlyPriceUsd`, and `FreebuffSubscriptionInfo` gains optional `source`, `billingInterval`, and `renewsAt` fields. Per the inline docblocks, purchasable and `yearlyPurchasable` gate whether the monthly Stripe price and annual checkout are configured, and `renewsAt` is the Stripe paid-through instant separate from the monthly usage reset.
ai.evidence: Commit [ebc17a50] adds `FREEBUFF_SUBSCRIPTION_BILLING_INTERVALS` (['monthly','yearly']) and `FreebuffSubscriptionBillingInterval` to `common/src/constants/freebuff-subscriptions.ts`, and adds optional `yearlyPriceUsd` to `FreebuffSubscriptionTierOffer` and optional `source`, `billingInterval`, `renewsAt` to `FreebuffSubscriptionInfo` in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show a consumer of the new billing interval fields or the `purchasable`/`yearlyPurchasable` flags, nor the rollout order relative to server-side Stripe price configuration.

ai.title: ADPOSTPAIDDEFAULTCREDITLINECENTS raised to 20000
ai.summary: AD_POSTPAID_DEFAULT_CREDIT_LINE_CENTS raised from 10000 to 20000. AD_POSTPAID_COLLECTION_THRESHOLD_CENTS added at 10000, enforcing that collection must start before the minimum credit line can stop delivery. AD_CREDIT_LINE_MIN_GROWTH_STEP_CENTS decoupled from default line, hardcoded to 10000. Scope limited to common/src/constants/freebuff-topups.ts.

eli5.text: When an advertiser on the postpaid plan saves their payment card for the first time, they now get a $200 starting credit line instead of $100 before any ads actually run. This higher starting limit only kicks in after the system confirms the card can be charged, so advertisers can't spend money they haven't yet been verified for. Additionally, the rules that increase credit limits later now use a fixed $100 minimum step that no longer changes if the default limit changes. These adjustments are already live today in the billing system.

entries.summary: New files: `common/src/types/gravity-showcase-experiment.ts`.

ai.title: Gravity Showcase experiment assignment and presentation telemetry
ai.summary: A new experiment module (`common/src/types/gravity-showcase-experiment.ts`) adds `gravityShowcaseConfig` and `gravityShowcaseAssignment`, which bucket users into treatment/control arms via a salted fnv1a hash keyed on `gravity_showcase_artwork_2026_09`, so the Gravity Showcase ad placement can be evaluated against a control group. The showcase presentation event (`ADS_SHOWCASE_PRESENTED = 'ads.showcase_presented'`) is added to the analytics enum and wired into the Axiom-only logging path, where `createGravityShowcasePresentationTelemetry` re-validates each client-reported presentation payload field-by-field and `getAxiomOnlyLogEvent` returns { event, data: data ?? {} }, keeping malformed rows in the restricted branch instead of retaining raw client input. Ingestion in `buildLogRows` re-runs the same validation and drops rows entirely when the user is anonymous, the event name is missing, or the telemetry fails validation, so malformed or unauthenticated showcase rows never reach the sink as raw client payloads.
ai.evidence: New file `common/src/types/gravity-showcase-experiment.ts` defines `GRAVITY_SHOWCASE_EXPERIMENT_VERSION` ('gravity-showcase-v1'), `GravityShowcaseExperimentArm`, `GravityShowcaseExperiment`, `GravityShowcaseAssignment`, `gravityShowcaseConfig`, and `gravityShowcaseAssignment` (which uses `ASSIGNMENT_SALT` = 'gravity_showcase_artwork_2026_09' and a local fnv1a to bucket user ids into treatment/control); `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts` adds `ADS_SHOWCASE_PRESENTED = 'ads.showcase_presented'`; `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` adds `ADS_SHOWCASE_PRESENTED_EVENT`, `SHOWCASE_PRESENTATION_VARIANTS`, `createGravityShowcasePresentationTelemetry` (returns Record<string, string> | null), and a new branch in `getAxiomOnlyLogEvent` returning { event, data: data ?? {} }; `common/src/util/log-ingest.ts` adds handling in `buildLogRows` that re-validates the showcase payload with `createGravityShowcasePresentationTelemetry` and returns `[]` for non-null userId, malformed telemetry, or missing identity (`common/src/util/__tests__/log-ingest.test.ts` asserts authenticated rows are kept with cleared identity fields while anonymous/malformed rows are dropped).
ai.unknowns: Whether a server-side caller actually invokes `gravityShowcaseAssignment` to emit `gravity_showcase_version`/`gravity_showcase_config_id`/`gravity_showcase_arm` onto client payloads, since the assignment logic and the telemetry re-validation are not concretely wired together in this diff. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.
